title: pkg/infra local conventions and gotchas
answers: Why do some pkg/infra loggers not have an infra. prefix?
Is InitTestDB still the right way to set up a test DB?
Can RegisterContextualLogProvider be called more than once?
Is the remotecache.CacheStorage doc comment accurate?
body:
- Logger-name prefixing (e.g. `infra.lockservice`, `infra.kvstore.sql`) is inconsistently applied — `tracing`, `pkg/infra/metrics/service.go`, and `httpclientprovider` all omit the `infra.` prefix. Check the local package rather than assuming a repo-wide naming rule.
- `log.RegisterContextualLogProvider` (`pkg/infra/log/log.go`) is a process-global additive slice; calling it twice (e.g. in ad-hoc test setup) duplicates log fields on every subsequent `FromContext` call.
- `db.InitTestDB`/`InitTestDBWithCfg` in `pkg/infra/db/db.go` are deprecated (`// Deprecated: use NewTestStore instead`, `//nolint:staticcheck`) but still used by older tests (`kvstore_test.go`, `serverlock_test.go`). New tests should use `db.NewTestStore`.
- `remotecache.CacheStorage`'s doc comment in `pkg/infra/remotecache/remotecache.go` references a `remotecache.Register(...)` function for gob encoding that no longer exists in the package — stale doc, don't trust it at face value.
- Repo-wide banned imports enforced via `.golangci.yml` `main` depguard also apply here: no `io/ioutil`, `gopkg.in/yaml.v2` or `v3`, `github.com/pkg/errors`, `github.com/xorcare/pointer`, `github.com/gofrs/uuid`.
applies: When adding logging, tests, or reading docs in pkg/infra subpackages specifically; not a repo-wide guarantee.
